Heart of Lozenets: the architect's pictures and Polycity's 3D map

The development is not built. Left is the architect's design, right is how Polycity draws the uploaded development today.

The whole plan from above

The towers by the park

The main square

Why they differ

  1. Shape. The file uploaded to Polycity keeps one outline per building, 51 in all, so every building stands straight. The architect's 3D model builds them from 440 pieces, 398 of them one floor tall, and its towers narrow floor by floor.
  2. Walls. The architect's model carries no wall materials, windows or balconies. Polycity places them from each building's outline, floors and use. Stone, brick and planted balconies exist only in the architect's pictures.
  3. Ground. The model's planted areas and stream were not carried into the uploaded file.

Other uploaded files are drawn the same way

Polycity reads a building model (IFC), a site plan (DXF) or its own development file, and draws every uploaded building by the same rules. A Rhino model or a DWG drawing is converted into one of those first, as the Lozenets model was.

Architect's pictures: Henning Larsen, The Heart of Lozenets, Technical Proposal, March 2026. Polycity's pictures: the editor's 3D map, 17 Nov 2026. The house and the site plan are sample files placed on a plot in Tallinn.
